questions.question_text:
A solid is a cylinder of radius $4$ cm and height $9$ cm with a cone of the same radius and height $6$ cm on top.
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used $\pi r^2 h$ for the cone too, forgetting its factor of one third.
Found only the cylinder and left out the cone.

questions.question_text:
A tank is a cylinder of radius $3$ cm and height $10$ cm capped by a hemisphere of the same radius.
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full sphere on top instead of a hemisphere.
Found only the cylinder and left out the hemisphere.

questions.question_text:
An ice-cream is a cone of radius $3$ cm and height $8$ cm topped with a hemisphere of the same radius.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used a full sphere on top instead of a hemisphere.
Used $\pi r^2 h$ for the cone, forgetting its factor of one third.

questions.question_text:
Two identical square-based pyramids are joined along their matching bases. Each pyramid has base side length $4$ cm and perpendicular height $9$ cm.
Find the total volume in cm³, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Found only one pyramid instead of two.
Used $Ah$ for each pyramid, leaving out the factor of one third.

questions.question_text:
A cone sits exactly inside a cylinder. Both have radius $6$ cm and perpendicular height $10$ cm.
What fraction of the volume of the cylinder is the cone?

options.why: Found the fraction of the cylinder outside the cone instead of the fraction taken up by the cone.
Divided the cylinder's volume by the cone's volume instead of the cone's volume by the cylinder's volume.

questions.question_text: A square-based pyramid of base side $6$ m and height $9$ m sits on top of a cube of edge $6$ m. Find the total volume of the solid in m³.

options.why: Left out the factor of one third on the pyramid (used $Ah$).
Found only the cube and left out the pyramid.

questions.question_text: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $1$ m and height $4$ m topped by a cone of the same radius and height $3$ m. Find its total volume in m³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the cylinder and left out the cone roof.
Used $\pi r^{2}h$ for the cone, leaving out the factor of one third.

questions.question_text:
A capsule is a cylinder of radius $3$ cm and height $5$ cm with a hemisphere on each end (together a full sphere).
Find its total volume in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Found only the cylinder's volume and left out both hemispheres.
Added only one hemisphere instead of two.
